gen_risks.description: Substantial environmental and social risks across sub-projects financed through financial intermediaries under ESS9.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply NAFIN and PFI Environmental and Social Management Systems, enforce a ring-fenced Exclusion List, perform due diligence on subprojects, and conduct World Bank sample verification.
gen_risks.evidence: Environmental and Social Risk Classification Substantial

gen_risks.description: SMEs and mid-cap firms lack internal technical capacity and knowledge to measure emissions, prepare bankable green projects, and comply with MRV frameworks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide firm-level technical assistance under Component 2, including funding for feasibility studies, market assessments, and support for preparing Sustainability Plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Most Mexican firms lack the capacity to measure emissions, implement energy-use, generation or management systems, and comply with reporting frameworks

gen_risks.description: Participating Financial Institutions and NAFIN face capacity constraints in designing, originating, appraising, and monitoring green and sustainability-linked loan products.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide structured capacity building and technical assistance to PFIs and NAFIN, including guidance documents, templates, calculation tools, and digital monitoring systems.
gen_risks.evidence: Mexican financial institutions are limited in their capacity to design, originate, appraise and monitor green loans and sustainable finance products.

gen_risks.description: Low demand or limited uptake of SLL and GL products by beneficiary enterprises due to transaction costs, administrative complexity, and uncertain payback periods.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer time-bound step-down pricing incentives, deploy direct technical assistance to lower transaction costs, and partner with anchor companies and industry associations to generate demand.
gen_risks.evidence: mitigate the risk of a situation where financing is available, but uptake is limited.

gen_risks.description: Risk of greenwashing or non-credible performance claims in Sustainability-Linked Sub-loans and Green Sub-loans.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate ex-ante validation of Sustainability Plans and ex-post verification of key performance indicators and targets by qualified, independent validation entities.
gen_risks.evidence: To mitigate the risk of greenwashing, targets and results in the SP will be subject to... ex-ante validation and ex-post verification

gen_risks.description: Extreme weather events and climate hazards (droughts, floods, heatwaves) could cause operational disruptions and increase loan delinquency rates among beneficiary enterprises.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize sub-project financing for energy reliability, water efficiency, and climate resilience technologies while embedding climate risk assessments in sub-loan appraisal.
gen_risks.evidence: Extreme temperatures have been shown to raise loan delinquency rates among Mexican firms

gen_risks.description: Foreign exchange risk exposure on NAFIN's balance sheet resulting from borrowing in USD and on-lending primarily in MXN.
gen_risks.mitigation: Manage currency exposure using local currency swap markets and limit USD sub-lending strictly to beneficiary enterprises with explicit natural export hedges.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will manage the FX risk on its own balance sheet using Mexico’s well developed currency swap market.

gen_risks.description: Credit and default risk exposure assumed by NAFIN on direct mid-cap sub-loans and on credit lines to Participating Financial Institutions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain robust credit risk margins, enforce PFI financial soundness criteria, set single-borrower exposure limits, and require minimum co-financing from borrowers and PFIs.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will assume the credit risk of the BEs when lending directly and of the PFIs on second-tier operations

gen_risks.description: NAFIN procurement staff lack direct experience in executing selection and contracting processes under World Bank Procurement Regulations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign a dedicated internal procurement professional, receive hands-on training from the World Bank, and implement close Bank oversight for initial procurement packages.
gen_risks.evidence: while NAFIN staff are familiar with the World Bank Procurement Regulations, they have not been directly involved in carrying out selection and contracting processes.

gen_risks.description: Financial management efficiency constraints and operational risks arising from reliance on legacy information systems requiring manual data consolidation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce established internal control mechanisms, perform regular supervisory reviews and reconciliations, and execute targeted internal audit coverage detailed in the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: efficiency constraints arising from reliance on legacy information systems requiring manual consolidation

gen_risks.description: Exclusion of Mexican SMEs and mid-caps from global value chains due to non-compliance with strict corporate Scope 3 emissions and sustainability standards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide tailored long-tenor financing and targeted TA to help firms adopt renewable energy, energy efficiency, and verified sustainability plans aligned with global anchor requirements.
gen_risks.evidence: Firms that do not comply risk forward-exclusion from supply chains, with implications for sales and employment

gen_risks.description: Potential delays to project effectiveness from required fulfillment of legal effectiveness conditions, including adoption of the POM and Sustainable Finance Framework.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize grant funds from the Grant Facility for Project Preparation (GFPP) to advance preparation and adoption of the POM and Sustainable Finance Framework prior to effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: The Additional Conditions of Effectiveness consist of... adoption of the Project Operations Manual... and Sustainable Finance Framework

gen_risks.description: Shallow local financial market conditions and short average SME loan tenors restrict private bank lending for long-term sustainability investments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide long-tenor IBRD and CCEFCF blended credit lines through NAFIN and PFIs with explicit minimum maturity rules established in the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: SME loans are mostly provided for short-term, working-capital purposes, with the average SME loan-tenor less than two years.

gt_risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

gt_risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
gt_risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

gt_risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
gt_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

gt_risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.
